title: Reduced fetal movements
summary: Any reported reduction, change, or absence of fetal movements from 24+0 weeks.
redFlags: No fetal movements felt at all — assess without delay, any time of day.
Recurrent presentation of reduced movements this pregnancy — itself a risk factor, even if movements are still present.

blocks.heading: No movements felt at all
bullets: Attend for immediate assessment — handheld Doppler check for fetal heartbeat is the first step.
If fetal heart cannot be confidently identified, arrange urgent ultrasound confirmation of viability without delay.
If fetal heart confirmed, proceed to full assessment per the recurrent/risk-factor pathway below (CTG plus growth/liquor/Doppler ultrasound) — VERIFY local escalation route.
Escalate to obstetric team immediately regardless of contact channel.

By phone: tell her to come in right away, do not wait — this needs checking now, whatever the time. If she has any other symptoms (bleeding, severe pain, feeling generally unwell/collapse), advise 999 instead of driving herself in.

blocks.heading: Recurrent presentation (reported before, this pregnancy)
bullets: Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG (VERIFY minimum duration locally — commonly at least 20 minutes).
Arrange ultrasound for growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Dopplers within 24 hours, regardless of CTG result — recurrent presentation is itself a risk factor.
Full clinical assessment: symphysis-fundal height, BP, urinalysis, review of risk factors.
Discuss with obstetric team given repeat presentation.
Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone).

blocks.heading: First presentation with risk factors present
bullets: Risk factors: small-for-gestational-age or growth concerns, known placental insufficiency, previous stillbirth, maternal diabetes, obstetric cholestasis, hypertensive disease, or reduced movements alongside any bleeding, pain, or reduced fluid.
Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG.
Arrange ultrasound for growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Dopplers within 24 hours given risk factors present.
Full clinical assessment including BP and urinalysis (pre-eclampsia screen) if not already done today.
Discuss with obstetric team.
Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone).

blocks.heading: First presentation, no additional risk factors, 24+ weeks
bullets: Confirm fetal heartbeat and perform CTG (VERIFY minimum duration locally — commonly at least 20 minutes).

If CTG is normal and no other concerns identified, growth ultrasound is not routinely required for a single first presentation at term with no risk factors — VERIFY local pathway, particularly for gestations under 28 weeks where practice may differ.
Full clinical assessment: symphysis-fundal height, BP, urinalysis.
Seen within 1 hour (face-to-face) / same-day assessment (phone).

blocks.heading: Under 24 weeks
bullets: Reassure that fetal movement patterns vary widely and are often not consistently felt before 24 weeks, especially in a first pregnancy.
If she has never felt any movement at all by 24 weeks, arrange assessment.
Provide general fetal-movement-awareness information.

blocks.heading: Safety-netting to give
bullets: Come back in immediately, any time, if movements reduce again or stop, or if bleeding, pain, headache/visual symptoms, or fever develop.
Contact the unit again at any time if worried, however many times, even if she has called before.
Continue to be aware of the baby's usual pattern of movements going forward.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: Time movements last definitely felt, and time of this contact.
Fetal heart confirmed by handheld Doppler — yes/no, by whom, at what time.
Number and dates of previous RFM presentations this pregnancy, if recurrent.
CTG findings and duration; growth scan booked — date/time.
Risk factors reviewed; advice and safety-netting given.
